docs/adr/0001-changesets-compatible-change-records.md:13:The human-written change record is a `.changeset/*.md` file in `@changesets/cli`'s format: YAML frontmatter mapping package names to `none`/`patch`/`minor`/`major`, then a Markdown summary. docs/architecture/versioning.md:16:- `ReleasePreview` (`crates/callisto-graph/src/release_preview.rs`) is the serializable, versioned view of a plan for people: packages, merged changes, bystanders and findings. Surfaces such as the PR body render it; they do not recompute from the plan. `version --emit-preview` writes it before apply consumes the changesets, and `compose-pr-body --preview` renders from that file. Each changeset change records `pr`, the pull request that added it, read from the first-parent merge commits in one `git log` when the history names one. `ReleasePreview` also carries findings from the changesets (a `Breaking:` or `Action:` marker, a breaking marker whose bump is too low, and no \"backward compatible\" claim when there is a breaking one) and `unreleased`, the publishable packages with source changes since their last tag that the plan does not bump (a package with no tag has no baseline and is not listed) (`version --emit-preview` computes it; a failure to look is a warning). `pr_labels()` derives the managed label catalog, with an `applied` flag per label, from the same findings. `--publish-plan` adds `publish`, the outcome of `plan_workspace_release_offline` on the versioned tree for exactly the packages the preview bumps (the committed decision holds those, not every unreleased package). It never observes a registry or the forge, so the checks that need one (a published version left behind, a name another project owns) are left to the release itself; a refusal becomes a `Stop` finding. `publish.versionedOnly` (optional, absent when empty) names the bumped packages with no publish target, such as a private fixed-group member, which are versioned but never published; the PR body lists them after the publish table. Rows are keyed by the qualified release identity, so `cargo/x` and `npm/x` stay apart.
docs/architecture/polyglot-v1.md:18:- Configuration, generated config, machine reports and command-line arguments use only canonical `cargo/name`, `npm/@scope/name` or `pypi/name` references; bare and colon-form aliases are rejected. Changesets and `pre.json` keep native package names, resolved when read, because an entry names an owner package and the files stay readable by `@changesets/cli`. Native normalization belongs to the ecosystem; Python distribution names are not import names, and a `pypi/` reference uses the declared name.
